title: The compact log-property path is default-axes-only by construction

decision.summary: The compact path — `LogPropertyCompact` and the compact branch of `LogEventBuffer.ToLogEvent` — accepts only properties whose three optional axes (`CaptureMode`, `Format`, `Visibility`) carry their default values. Properties with non-default axes take the full `LogProperty` path. This is a contract, not a limitation.
decision.rationale: The compact path is the hot path. It is narrow because narrow is fast. Widening the compact struct to carry the three optional axes costs roughly 4% on the synchronous accept path at the 8-property EPICS arity; on Jared's bench rig the noise band on those measurements is ~8 ns on 45 ns numbers, wider than the 3 ns delta the widening would introduce. Paying real structural complexity for a perf cost that disappears into noise is the wrong trade. The full `LogProperty` path is the right home for non-default-axis properties, and the API surface today already routes them there.

contract.statement: Any property reachable by the compact path carries default `CaptureMode`, default `Format`, and default `Visibility`. Properties that need non-default axes flow through the full `LogProperty` path. `LogPropertyCompact.ToLogProperty()` is lossy-in-shape but not lossy-in-data — the call signature drops three nullable parameters, and the inputs that reach the compact path are guaranteed to have those parameters at their default.
in-scope: `LogPropertyCompact(string name, object? value)` — the only public constructor today
`LogPropertyCompact.From<T>(string name, T value)` — the factory today
`LogEventBuffer.ToLogEvent()` compact branch — emits the buffered compacts as `LogProperty` instances with default axes
out-of-scope: Properties marked `PiiSensitive` — force-eager to the full path before they reach a compact slot

alternatives-considered.name: Widen `LogPropertyCompact` to carry the three axes
alternatives-considered.summary: Add `CaptureMode?`, `Format?`, `Visibility?` fields to the compact struct so it carries the full `LogProperty` semantics losslessly.
alternatives-considered.measured-cost: ~4% on the synchronous accept path at 8-property EPICS arity. Jared's bench rig shows ~8 ns noise band on 45 ns measurements; the 3 ns delta the widening would add sits inside that band. The cost is real on the structure side and unmeasurable on the perf side — paying complexity for noise is the wrong trade.

alternatives-considered.name: Per-event sparse-optional axes-override `[InlineArray]` sidecar on `LogEventBuffer`
alternatives-considered.summary: Mirror the existing `EventId` and `GenSource` sparse-optional precedent — keep the compact struct narrow, attach the axes only on events that need them, via an `[InlineArray]` sidecar slot on `LogEventBuffer`. Most events allocate nothing in the sidecar; the rare event that needs non-default axes pays the small per-event sparse cost.
alternatives-considered.measured-cost: Not measured. Mirrors a shape already shipping (`EventId`, `GenSource`) so the perf envelope is bounded by that precedent. Not implemented today because the API surface does not yet expose the need.

alternatives-considered.name: Two parallel public APIs — a compact and a full constructor on `LogPropertyCompact`
alternatives-considered.summary: Expose `LogPropertyCompact(string, object?, CaptureMode?, Format?, Visibility?)` alongside the narrow form, and silently widen the struct when the richer constructor is called.
alternatives-considered.measured-cost: Not measured. Rejected on shape grounds: the narrow struct's `Size = 16` invariant is the whole point of the compact path; a constructor that violates the invariant is a footgun. A future need is better served by Option-7a, which keeps the invariant.

enforcement.xml-doc: `LogPropertyCompact` and `LogEventBuffer.ToLogEvent` carry XML-doc remarks naming the contract: compact path is default-axes-only by construction; non-default-axis properties take the full `LogProperty` path.

analyzer-rules.detects: A `LogProperty` instance whose `CaptureMode`, `Format`, or `Visibility` is non-default is passed to a compact-path API (`LogPropertyCompact` factory or a `LogEventBuffer` compact-slot write).
analyzer-rules.cannot-detect: Non-default axes assigned through reflection or through a runtime-generated `LogProperty` factory whose body the analyzer cannot read.

enforcement.strict-mode: `<HeraldStrictMode>true</HeraldStrictMode>` escalates HERALD014 to an error via the existing HRLD0002 mechanism. No new code on the escalation side.

true-by-construction: Every property reachable through `LogPropertyCompact(string, object?)` carries default axes — the constructor accepts no axis parameters
Every property reachable through `LogPropertyCompact.From<T>(string, T)` carries default axes — the factory accepts no axis parameters
`LogPropertyCompact.ToLogProperty()` produces a `LogProperty` whose three optional fields are at their defaults, because the source struct has nowhere to carry non-default values
enforced-by-analyzer: HERALD014: non-default-axis `LogProperty` passed to a compact-path API
documented-contract: A consumer who builds a `LogProperty` with non-default axes uses the full `LogProperty` path. The compact-path APIs do not accept it, and the analyzer flags the attempt at build time.
out-of-scope: Modification of Herald.OSS source to widen the compact struct or relax the analyzer — closed by consumer build provenance, not by library defense.

honest-residual.summary: The contract is total today because the API surface makes it total. The compact-path APIs accept no axis parameters; there is no public path that delivers a non-default-axis property into a compact slot. A future API change that exposed axes on the compact path would break the contract — the analyzer rule lives to catch that change at build time and force the conversation.
honest-residual.future-shape: If a real consumer need arrives for non-default axes on compact (the canonical case Richard named: a downstream processor wanting forensic-Silent on a compact buffer), the extension is Option-7a — the per-event sparse-optional axes-override sidecar on `LogEventBuffer`. The compact struct itself stays narrow.

extension-path.summary: When non-default axes on compact become a real shipping need, Option-7a attaches the axes to `LogEventBuffer` as a sparse-optional `[InlineArray]` sidecar, mirroring the existing `EventId` and `GenSource` precedent. Most events allocate nothing in the sidecar; the rare event that needs non-default axes pays a small per-event sparse cost. The compact struct's `Size = 16` invariant holds. The hot path stays the hot path.
extension-path.does-not-widen: `LogPropertyCompact` itself remains a 16-byte struct. The sidecar lives on `LogEventBuffer`, attached only when an event needs it.

interactions.interaction: `PiiSensitive` force-eager resolves a marked property to a full `LogProperty` (string-ified) on the producer thread before the property reaches a compact slot. PII never rides the compact path. The trust boundary in the PII posture and the contract here close in the same direction — both by construction.

The compact path is the data shape that makes the kernel path fast. Keeping the compact struct narrow is what keeps the kernel-path number (0.3 ns, zero allocations) achievable. The chain path takes the full `LogProperty` and pays the cost of the axes its decorators read.

pr-back-welcomed: If a contributor finds an elegant way to make the compact path carry non-default axes losslessly without the ~4% accept-path cost — or finds that the cost is genuinely zero on real hardware and the bench noise hid a real signal — they are welcome to open a PR. Show the measurement, show the shape, and we evaluate. The contract is what we ship today; the door is not closed.
